Concerning his own presence, which occurred in this world with flesh, that 'In that time, says the Lord, giving my laws into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts.' And rightly, the all-wise Paul, understanding this, writes to those who have obtained it, 'Our letter is you, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God.' Therefore, listen to me, he says, that is, receive my words, and do not become like Israel, who were hardened, adhering to the oldness of the written law, and seeing nothing from the types. Until the time of correction, the commandment given through Moses is established, he says. But since the time of the incarnation is not awaited, but has already come, the shadow should move towards the truth. Hear me, my people. Saying 'my people', he shows the spiritual affinity given to them at that time, entreating, as it seems, and through this, making them more eager to receive the word from him. He calls not only those who are among the people, but also kings, so that you may understand the rulers or the leaders of the people. For from the multitude of believers, many were brought to this, of whom the divine disciples were the firstfruits; then, following them, those who were named after the kingdom; and, having been enriched with the name of the kingdom, they were also appointed to lead the people.

And so, as from great joy, they stretch out more grateful hymns to God, saying: 'He has put peoples under us and nations under our feet.' The divine Singer also sings about them, saying: 'The rulers of peoples have gathered with the God of Abraham.' Oh, peoples and kings, he says, listen to me and pay attention, and what is the future promise? The law will go out from me, and my judgment will be a light to the nations. The divine and evangelical message is called a proclamation. For it is new and different, like a new and saving oracle, but also a change of the old law for the better, and a transition of types that have run their course to the truth. Christ said: 'Do not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill. For I say to you, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the law until all is fulfilled.' But the law in writing was given through Moses; the saving proclamation, that is, the evangelical message, went out through Christ. And it was fitting that Moses became a servant of the shadow and type, as it were, of knowledge and true worship.
pass_b_english: The Lord says, concerning his own presence, which occurred in this world with flesh, 'In that time, I will give my laws into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts' (Jeremiah 31:33).
The all-wise Paul, understanding this, writes to those who have obtained it, 'Our letter is you, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God' (2 Corinthians 3:3).
Therefore, hear me, that is, receive my words, and do not become like Israel, who were hardened and adhered to the oldness of the written law, seeing nothing from the types.
The commandment given through Moses is established until the time of correction, but since the time of the incarnation is not awaited, but has already come, the shadow should move towards the truth.

Hear me, my people, and receive the spiritual affinity given to you at this time, as the Lord calls not only those who are among the people, but also kings, so that you may understand the rulers or the leaders of the people.

From the multitude of believers, many were brought to this, of whom the divine disciples were the firstfruits; then, following them, those who were named after the kingdom; and, having been enriched with the name of the kingdom, they were also appointed to lead the people.

The people of God, filled with great joy, offer more grateful hymns to Him, proclaiming that He has put peoples under us and nations under our feet, saying, 'He has put peoples under us and nations under our feet' (Psalm 47:3).
The divine Singer also joins in, singing about the gathering of the rulers of peoples with the God of Abraham, saying, 'The rulers of peoples have gathered with the God of Abraham' (Psalm 47:9).

The Lord calls out to the peoples and kings, urging them to listen and pay attention to the promise of the future, declaring that His law will go out from Him, and His judgment will be a light to the nations.

The divine and evangelical message is a proclamation that brings a new and saving oracle, one that changes the old law for the better and transitions the types that have run their course to the truth.

Christ Himself said, 'Do not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill' (Matthew 5:17), and, 'Not one iota or one stroke will pass from the law until all is fulfilled' (Matthew 5:18).

The law in writing was given through Moses, but the saving proclamation, the evangelical message, went out through Christ, and it was fitting that Moses became a servant of the shadow and type, as it were, of knowledge and true worship.
